summary.oneLiner: FY26 was a deliberate de-risking year: JLG (microfinance) book cut from ~88% of loans (FY20) to ~28-30% now, secured lending raised to 51% of book, and legacy MFI stress (post the ~1.5-year MFIN 2.0 guardrail shock) is now clearing — fresh slippages fell from ~₹710cr (Q4FY25) to ~₹170cr (Q4FY26) and GNPA improved ~330bps QoQ to 7.7%. Bank still posted a Q4 net loss of ₹188cr on legacy provisioning, but management calls "worst behind us," guides to FY27 as a consolidation year and FY28 exit ROE >15%.

one-line thesis: FY26 was a deliberate de-risking year: JLG (microfinance) book cut from ~88% of loans (FY20) to ~28-30% now, secured lending raised to 51% of book, and legacy MFI stress (post the ~1.5-year MFIN 2.0 guardrail shock) is now clearing — fresh slippages fell from ~₹710cr (Q4FY25) to ~₹170cr (Q4FY26) and GNPA improved ~330bps QoQ to 7.7%. Bank still posted a Q4 net loss of ₹188cr on legacy provisioning, but management calls "worst behind us," guides to FY27 as a consolidation year and FY28 exit ROE >15%.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs called out: FY26 PPoP was depressed by ~₹84cr of cumulative interest-reversal on fresh slippages (adjusted PPoP ~₹140cr vs reported ₹56cr); a one-time charge from new Labour Codes/LTIP/ESOP grants hit in Q3FY26 with incremental spillover into Q4FY26.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Loan book growth: 25–30% p.a. over "coming years" (medium-term target reiterated on call).
Secured mix: target ~55% of gross loan book (vs 51% now, 43% a year ago).
NIM: >8% (medium-term target).
ROE: ~15% target; FY28 exit ROE "above 15%" reconfirmed on this call (from prior-call guidance).
Credit cost: reiterated from previous call — ~3–3.5% FY27, 2–2.5% FY28 (management flags this as conservative given slippage trajectory and CGFMU cover).
Net NPA: <1% by FY28 (from ~3.3% in FY26).
New CBS (core banking system) launch targeted Q2/Q3 FY27 (part of "Utkarsh 2.0" tech transformation).
Capital raise: no immediate equity capital raise planned; if needed, will use Tier-2 or balance-sheet monetization, not equity market.
Reverse merger (holding co. UCL into the bank): 2nd motion petition filed with NCLT 5-Apr-2026; expected to complete "in the next few months," subject to NCLT.
FY27 explicitly framed as a consolidation year — converting Q4FY26 green shoots into sustained momentum, not a growth-acceleration year.
order book & pipeline: Disbursement momentum turning: JLG disbursements +58% QoQ (+2% YoY) to ₹1,310cr in Q4FY26 — first QoQ increase after 3 consecutive quarters of decline — as collections stabilized (~Oct/Nov-25) and sales focus resumed under MFIN 2.0 guardrails; management still describes disbursal capacity as running at only ~70% of optimum, implying further upside. Non-JLG disbursements +41% QoQ / +51% YoY. MBBL (graduating-JLG secured-adjacent product) +122% YoY / +40% QoQ, now 27% of micro-banking book with <15% penetration — flagged as the biggest headroom item.
segment / subsidiary detail: MSME: book +15% YoY to ₹4,456cr; new Micro LAP sub-segment yielding ~18% disbursement; MSME GNPA improved to 3.4% (from 3.6% prior quarter); largely secured by hard collateral (residential/commercial).
BBG (Business Banking Group): fully secured against immovable collateral, +19% YoY.

CV/CE ("Wheels"): book -1% QoQ to ₹1,090cr; deliberate mix shift toward used vehicles (share of disbursements ~30% in FY26 vs <15% a year ago) as new-vehicle financing was showing riskier behaviour; Wheels remains the main driver of elevated non-MFI slippages (~4%), expected to normalize over "at least another 2 quarters."
Deposits: total deposits +0.4% YoY / ~+3% QoQ (broadly stable by design); retail term deposits +20% YoY; CASA +11% YoY/+13% QoQ; CASA+RTD ratio 83% (Mar-26) vs 71% (Mar-25); CASA ratio 24%.
growth verticals / optionality: MBBL scale-up (27% of micro-banking book, <15% penetration) — largest identified growth lever within the de-risked JLG-graduate segment.
Gold Loan — new-ish product, management expects meaningfully bigger scale this year.

Post-Q3FY26 write-off/NPA recovery vertical: ~30% of the 1,200+ collection headcount to be redeployed toward legacy write-off/NPA collection once fresh-slippage normalization completes; ₹50cr collected from NPA/write-off pool in Q4FY26 alone (~20% of collected value via a ~900-person team then).
6a. moat & competitive position: CGFMU credit-guarantee coverage: ~70% of the microfinance book (counting Q4FY26 disbursements) now covered under the credit-guarantee scheme (registered effective 17-Jan-2025) — reduces incremental portfolio risk on new MFI-book originations; management stresses no accounting/capital benefit has yet been booked from this cover (pure cost so far), so any future claim/capital-relief is unrecognized upside.
Deep micro-finance underwriting experience (per management) supporting confidence in resuming 25-30% growth from a low base without repeating past credit-cost cycles.
margins & cost dynamics: Cost of funds down to 7.9% in Q4FY26 (from 8.3% in Q4FY25, 8.1% in Q3FY26) via calibrated deposit repricing after RBI repo cuts; further reduction expected as repricing continues. Reported FY26 PPoP (₹56cr) heavily suppressed by interest-income reversals from fresh slippages (~₹84cr across the year); management expects reversals to shrink as the new (post-guardrail) disbursement book performs and collection efficiency holds, allowing steady-state interest income to "find its revival" over the next ~4 quarters.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): New CBS (core banking system) launch targeted Q2/Q3 FY27 as part of "Utkarsh 2.0" technology transformation (digital underwriting, 360-degree control-parameter mapping).

Collections infrastructure already built out: workforce for JLG/MBBL collections expanded to >1,200 as of Mar-26; specialized call center for overdue accounts; larger micro-banking branches split for better oversight.
capital allocation: Rights issue of ₹950cr completed Nov-2025 to strengthen Tier-1 capital.
ARC sale of stressed JLG portfolio executed to clean up legacy stress off the balance sheet.
No immediate plans for further equity capital raise (CRAR 17.7%); if a shortfall emerges, management prefers Tier-2 capital or balance-sheet monetization over tapping equity markets.
Reverse merger of holding company UCL into the bank in progress (NCLT process).
risks & watch-items: Legacy MFI/JLG stress still being provided for: 85% and ~70% provisioning stages still remaining on some aging buckets per CRO — implies further (declining) provisioning drag over the next couple of quarters.
Wheels (CV/CE) segment remains the main source of non-MFI slippages (~4%); expected to normalize only over "another 2 quarters."

ECL/Ind AS transition: SFBs currently exempted (implementation from 1-Apr-2027 excludes SFBs); management notes its own pro-forma Ind AS provisioning could be equal to or higher than current levels when/if it eventually applies — a future overhang, not immediate.

Geopolitical: management monitored Iran-Israel/Middle East tensions (~2.5 months) for MSME export-exposure risk; states no abnormal portfolio behavior seen so far (ticket sizes too small for meaningful export/forex exposure).
Credit-cost guidance (3–3.5% FY27, 2–2.5% FY28) explicitly reiterated (not raised) despite improving trends — management calling its own guidance "conservative," a point to verify against actuals.
management quality / tone: Candid and granular in Q&A (specific PCR splits by book, SARFAESI timelines, LTV/risk-weight detail, opex-per-growth math). Repeated emphasis on not having booked any accounting/capital benefit yet from CGFMU cover — a conservative disclosure stance. Tone: cautiously confident ("worst is behind us"), explicitly reframing FY27 as consolidation rather than re-acceleration, which reads as credible expectation-setting rather than promotional.
non-obvious takeaways: The ₹56cr reported vs ~₹140cr adjusted PPoP gap (FY26) is a clean, quantified bridge management gave unprompted — useful reconciliation item for modeling next year's PPoP recovery.

CGFMU cover (~70% of MFI book) is running as a pure cost today (premium expensed, zero benefit taken in NPA recognition or capital adequacy) — a hidden capital/provisioning optionality if/when claims mature (~1.5-year claim cycle per management).
Reverse merger of parent UCL into the bank is progressing (NCLT 2nd motion filed Apr-2026) — corporate-structure simplification event to track for completion timing.

Collection headcount (1,200+) is a temporary asset being explicitly repurposed toward write-off/NPA recovery (not just fresh-slippage collection) as normalization completes — an underappreciated future "collection ROI" lever (₹50cr recovered in Q4FY26 alone from ~900 people).
challenges → beneficiaries & losers (lis: No listed-stock beneficiary/loser could be resolved against our own companies.csv/products.csv or StockMetadata.csv for the challenges discussed on this call (MFIN 2.0 guardrail-driven MFI industry slowdown, CGFMU credit-guarantee cost, Middle-East geopolitical monitoring for MSME exporters, deferred ECL/Ind AS transition for SFBs) — these are largely self-referential/industry-structural points rather than named-competitor or named-supplier dynamics. Left blank per rule (no invented names).
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (this): Fresh slippages collapsed (~₹710cr→~₹170cr YoY); GNPA improved 330bps QoQ to 7.7%; JLG mix down to 28–30% of book; secured mix up to 51%; net loss ₹188cr on legacy provisioning; Rights issue (₹950cr, Nov-25) done; reverse merger (UCL into bank) filed with NCLT; FY27 framed as consolidation year; credit-cost guidance (3–3.5% FY27 / 2–2.5% FY28) and FY28 ROE >15% reiterated.

Q1 FY27 → check: Did JLG/non-JLG disbursement momentum (+58%/+41% QoQ) continue or was Q4 a one-off low-base bounce? Did fresh slippages keep falling below ~₹170cr/qtr? Any progress on CBS launch (guided Q2/Q3 FY27) and NCLT reverse-merger completion? Any change to "no equity raise" stance despite 25–30% growth ambition?
